chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Amr al-Nakha'i, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Hasten with charity, for the affliction does not bypass it.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity/alms beyond what is obligatory; distinct from zakat
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: Bala' — affliction, calamity, tribulation; includes illness, hardship, and divine tests
key_terms.بَكِّرُوا: Hasten early (from bakara, to do something at dawn/early); implies urgency and promptness

ai.seo_question: Does giving charity protect against affliction in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) encouraging Muslims to give sadaqah (voluntary charity) early and promptly. The hadith asserts that affliction and calamity cannot pass by or overcome the barrier created by charitable giving — a foundational teaching in Islamic spirituality on the protective power of sadaqah. This was understood by the early Muslim community as encouraging charitable giving before hardship strikes, as a prophylactic against misfortune.
